title: Charles Hémard de Denonville, cardinal de Mâcon, Rome and Orvieto to Anne de Montmorency, 1536-37, in Mascon's cipher (BnF fr. 3053, DECODE R4233-R4247; BnF fr. 3071 no. 4)

steps.what: fr. 3071 no. 4: transcribed the Mâcon letter's cipher (f. 9r ll. 3-34, f. 9v) at glyph level into aliases, in parallel parts (fr3071_no4/aliases/).
fr. 3071 no. 4: built macon_key.md from Lasry's table for fr. 3071 f. 9 and Tomokiyo's fr. 3053 tables, and applied it with macon_decode.py.

fr. 3071 no. 4: read the cipher apart from short spots on f. 9r (about 90 % then; f. 9r ll. 26-34 ~175 of ~190 signs, f. 9v ll. 1-16 in full); identified the code numbers 20/30/40 = Empereur/pape/roy, absent from the published tables.
fr. 3071 no. 4: the slip f. 9bis is a contemporary decipherment of the f. 9v passage and matches the reading made first almost word for word.

Correction from George Lasry: he decoded the fr. 3071 no. 4 letter (with the other three of catalogue item 6) in 2023 when reconstructing the key, unpublished; learned of after the reading and not used.
Checked Tomokiyo's francis.htm, Lasry's GL.htm, DECODE's sixteen fr. 3053 records and the Dodieu edition table for a published decipherment
Identified the catalogue's 'unknown sender' as the cardinal de Mâcon from Tomokiyo's description of the volume and from the clear signatures on R4239, R4240 and R4247
Fetched the sixteen record pages and the images of the eight target records from DECODE with the stored cookie
Applied 'Mascon's cipher' (macon_key.md, built in gramont1529 from Lasry's and Tomokiyo's tables) to the cipher lines
Glyph-level transcription of the cipher passages of all eight records by reading agents, one or two records at a time
Six contemporary marginal or interlinear decipherments found in the volume; three agree with the independent decoding word for word
Corrected the working table from a glossed line ('quant au faict de florence'): the big curly X is Q/U, not N, and the QUE group is written three ways
Read R4240 (~85%), R4247 letter 1 (~80%), R4238 (~65%), R4233 (~60%), passages of R4235 and R4239, and 66 lines of R4234
Third pass, two reading agents at a time: R4234 P8-P12 (~58 lines) and P16-P20 (~30 lines, P15 a clear copy of P16 used as crib), with the corrected glyph values
Fetched DECODE's un-downloaded full-page views of R4234 (P4, P7, P10, P13, P14, P18) to check for a missing page: all duplicate the crops
R4235 P2-P3 (29 lines, ~80%) and passage D on P8 aligned with the contemporary clear copy on P6 (~92%); R4247 letter 2 (27 lines, ~75%, last six in fragments)
R4239 P3-P15, the 100 unread lines (~72%), with the clear text of P18-P22 as a running crib
Opened the eight sibling DECODE records R4236-R4246 via the API: all status Decrypted with no plaintext file attached; outside catalogue 180, not read

Searched Ribier 1666, Dodieu, nunciature editions and BnF copy collections for clear copies of the eight letters; found none, but found fr. 3053 on Gallica at native resolution and Mâcon's companion letter to the King of 15 Feb 1537 with its contemporary decipherment (Dupuy 44, ff. 30-38)

Segmented and clustered 1,262 glyphs by shape: the readers' single alias for the barred crosses is four or five distinct key signs (O, U/V, P, F, M); LM lattice decoding over old aliases cut CER 14.4% -> 9.2% on ground-truth lines
Pilot shape-true re-transcription with a sign catalogue: CER on ground-truth lines 9.2% -> 5.8%
Dupuy 44 companion letter transcribed as a content crib; confirmed 'Vitelle' at the end of R4235 passage D; its proposed 'que luy a fait faire' rejected by the signs
Pass 5: every record re-transcribed sign by sign from Gallica native scans with baseline straightening, decoded by key map + fr-1600-letters beam
Found ff. 37r-v are a contemporary clear copy of R4239 letter 2; CER vs all clear texts: R4234 6.5%, R4235 6.4%, R4239 6.1% (f38v 3.1%), R4240 3.8%, R4233 8.3% (mostly spelling variants)
Pass-5 coverage: R4233 ~95%, R4234 ~94%, R4235 ~96.5%, R4238 ~94%, R4239 ~94%, R4240 ~98.5%, R4247 ~98%; R4247's 'faded' tail sharp on the Gallica scan; 'Lodes' = Lodi, not Rodez

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R4248 (fr. 3053 f. 85, a second, unrelated cipher read from its contemporary decipherment on f. 86) moved to its own entry targets/r4248/; the cardinal's letter of 11 Apr 1537 (fr. 3071 no. 4, Mascon's cipher, read 18 Sept 2026 under gramont1529) moved here with its key files, so this entry holds every document read in Mascon's cipher.

outcome.method_basis: 'Mascon's cipher' was reconstructed from fr. 3053 by Tomokiyo and tabulated by Lasry (2023, GL.htm, for fr. 3071 f. 9); the project applied it through macon_key.md to the seven fr. 3053 records and the fr. 3071 no. 4 letter, and corrected values from glossed lines in the volume.

gaps.item: residue inside read lines, ~5% of letters (listed per record in NOTES)
gaps.detail: ink legible on Gallica natives; ambiguous sign runs (7 = N/B, 4 = C/R, O/U) with no clear copy or gloss

gaps.item: R4239 short runs f36r L01-L06, f35v L27-L31; f38v L4 end, L8 end, margin block
gaps.detail: not resolved in pass 5; no clear copy; f38v interlinear does not fit the signs

gaps.item: proper names (For[?], Mer[?]le, Christofle's surname, two German captains, Cesane, Palmier)
gaps.detail: spelled in cipher but not settled to known names
doubtful in the contemporary clear copy itself

gaps.item: fr. 3071 no. 4: seven signs on f. 9r ll. 27-28, the word before 'puissance', the name group on f. 9r l. 8; clear text read loosely
gaps.detail: blot and odd signs on the Gallica scan; no gloss for f. 9r (the slip covers f. 9v only)

outcome.fraction_read_source: Letter-weighted after pass 5 on the fr. 3053 records: R4233 1,904/2,006; R4234 ~0.94 of 5,369; R4235 2,035/2,108; R4238 767/812; R4239 ~0.94 of 4,925; R4240 829/842; R4247 3,098/3,140. fr. 3071 no. 4 (about 840 signs, ~820 decoded by the readers' counts) does not move the figure. Confident letters counted per line on the LM output; CER against contemporary clear copies 3-8% (mostly spelling variants).
outcome.notes: About 95% of the cipher letters of the seven fr. 3053 records read after a shape-true re-transcription from the Gallica native scans (pass 5, 22 Sept 2026), checked against every contemporary clear text (CER 3-8%); the fr. 3071 no. 4 letter of 11 Apr 1537 read apart from short spots, its f. 9v passage confirmed by the contemporary slip f. 9bis. Nothing is physically unreadable in fr. 3053; the residue is ambiguous sign runs and names. Key recovered (Tomokiyo/Lasry Mascon's cipher, corrected and split by sign shape). R4248, in another cipher, is targets/r4248/.

credits.note: re-tabulation of Mascon's cipher, table dated 05/11/2023 for BnF fr. 3071 f. 9, on Tomokiyo's GL.htm
decoded the fr. 3071 no. 4 letter in 2023, never published (his correction of 21 Sept 2026); not the fr. 3053 records
clear copies and marginal/interlinear decipherments in fr. 3053 used as anchors; slip f. 9bis of fr. 3071 deciphers the f. 9v passage

prior.where: Contemporary marginal and interlinear decipherments of some fr. 3053 passages in the volume itself, and the slip f. 9bis deciphering the f. 9v passage of fr. 3071 no. 4. No printed or online plaintext: Tomokiyo and Lasry publish the key only. Lasry also decoded fr. 3071 no. 4 in 2023, unpublished (Lasry, 21 Sept 2026); no Lasry decipherment of the fr. 3053 letters is recorded.

human: nothing beyond setting the target; the DECODE session cookie already in the repository served the images
